data.name: SpfMissingTitle
data.value: No SPF record

data.name: SpfMissingRisk
data.value: Receiving servers cannot tell which servers may send mail for the domain, so forged messages are easier to deliver.

data.name: SpfMissingFix
data.value: Publish one TXT record starting with v=spf1 that lists the servers sending your mail (your provider gives the include) and ends with -all, or ~all while testing. If the domain sends no mail, publish v=spf1 -all.

data.name: SpfMultipleTitle
data.value: More than one SPF record

data.name: SpfMultipleRisk
data.value: With more than one SPF record the check ends with a permanent error, so SPF gives no protection at all.

data.name: SpfMultipleFix
data.value: Merge the records into a single TXT record starting with v=spf1.

data.name: SpfAllPassTitle
data.value: SPF authorizes any server (+all)

data.name: SpfAllPassRisk
data.value: Any server on the internet passes the SPF check for the domain, so SPF gives no protection.

data.name: SpfAllNeutralTitle
data.value: SPF does not reject other servers (?all or no all)

data.name: SpfAllNeutralRisk
data.value: Mail from servers that are not listed is treated as neutral, so SPF does not help against forged messages.

data.name: SpfAllFix
data.value: End the record with -all, or ~all while you check that every legitimate server is listed.

data.name: SpfTooManyLookupsTitle
data.value: SPF needs more than 10 DNS lookups

data.name: SpfTooManyLookupsRisk
data.value: Above 10 lookups the SPF check ends with a permanent error, so legitimate mail can fail SPF and DMARC.

data.name: SpfTooManyLookupsFix
data.value: Remove the include entries of services you no longer use, replace a and mx with ip4/ip6 ranges, or ask your providers for a lighter include.

data.name: SpfSyntaxErrorTitle
data.value: SPF record with a term that is not valid

data.name: SpfSyntaxErrorRisk
data.value: A term that is not valid makes the SPF check end with a permanent error, so SPF gives no protection.

data.name: SpfSyntaxErrorFix
data.value: Correct or remove the term shown in the evidence; if it is in a record of your provider, report it to them.

data.name: SpfBrokenReferenceTitle
data.value: SPF include or redirect to a domain without a valid SPF record

data.name: SpfBrokenReferenceRisk
data.value: An include or redirect that leads nowhere (or loops) makes the SPF check end with a permanent error.

data.name: SpfBrokenReferenceFix
data.value: Correct the domain name in the include or redirect, or remove it if the service is no longer used.

data.name: SpfUnverifiedTitle
data.value: SPF include that could not be checked

data.name: SpfUnverifiedRisk
data.value: The DNS did not answer for an included domain: if the error persists, receivers may get a temporary error too.

data.name: SpfUnverifiedFix
data.value: Run the check again later; if the error persists, check the included domain with its provider.

data.name: SpfPtrTitle
data.value: SPF uses the deprecated ptr mechanism

data.name: SpfPtrRisk
data.value: ptr is slow and unreliable: the standard says not to use it, and some receivers ignore it.

data.name: SpfPtrFix
data.value: Replace ptr with the ip4/ip6 ranges or the a/mx of the sending servers; if it is in a record of your provider (see the evidence), report it to them.

data.name: DmarcMissingTitle
data.value: No DMARC record

data.name: DmarcMissingRisk
data.value: Anyone can send mail that claims to come from the domain, and receivers have no policy telling them to block it.

data.name: DmarcMissingFix
data.value: Publish a TXT record at _dmarc.<your domain>, for example v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:<address>. Read the reports for 2-4 weeks, then move to p=quarantine and p=reject.

data.name: DmarcInvalidTitle
data.value: DMARC record not valid

data.name: DmarcInvalidRisk
data.value: Receivers ignore a DMARC record that is not valid (or more than one record), so the domain is not protected.

data.name: DmarcInvalidFix
data.value: Publish exactly one record at _dmarc.<your domain> that starts with v=DMARC1 and has a valid p tag (none, quarantine or reject).

data.name: DmarcNoneTitle
data.value: DMARC in monitoring mode (p=none)

data.name: DmarcNoneRisk
data.value: Anyone can send email on behalf of the domain without it being blocked.

data.name: DmarcNoneFix
data.value: Move the policy to p=quarantine after 2-4 weeks of clean reports, then to p=reject.

data.name: DmarcPartialTitle
data.value: DMARC policy applied to only {0}% of the messages (pct)

data.name: DmarcPartialRisk
data.value: Part of the forged mail is still delivered as if there were no policy.

data.name: DmarcPartialFix
data.value: Raise pct to 100, or remove the tag.

data.name: DmarcNoReportsTitle
data.value: DMARC without aggregate reports (rua)

data.name: DmarcNoReportsRisk
data.value: Without reports you cannot see who sends mail in the name of the domain, so tightening the policy is a blind step.

data.name: DmarcNoReportsFix
data.value: Add rua=mailto:<address> to the DMARC record, with a mailbox or a service that reads the reports.

data.name: DmarcSubdomainNoneTitle
data.value: Subdomains not protected by DMARC (sp=none)

data.name: DmarcSubdomainNoneRisk
data.value: Forged mail from made-up subdomains (for example billing.<your domain>) is not blocked.

data.name: DmarcSubdomainNoneFix
data.value: Set sp=quarantine or sp=reject, or remove sp so that subdomains follow p.

data.name: DkimNotFoundTitle
data.value: No DKIM key found on the common selectors

data.name: DkimNotFoundRisk
data.value: Without DKIM, messages can be altered on the way and DMARC can rely only on SPF, which breaks when mail is forwarded.

data.name: DkimNotFoundFix
data.value: Enable DKIM signing at your mail provider and publish its key. If DKIM is already active with another selector (see the DKIM-Signature header, tag s=), run the check again with that selector.

data.name: DkimUnreadableTitle
data.value: DKIM key that cannot be read (selector {0})

data.name: DkimUnreadableRisk
data.value: Receivers cannot verify the signatures made with this selector.

data.name: DkimUnreadableFix
data.value: Publish the key again exactly as given by the provider; a long key must be split into strings of at most 255 characters inside one TXT record.

data.name: DkimWeakKeyTitle
data.value: DKIM key too short (selector {0}, {1} bit)

data.name: DkimWeakKeyRisk
data.value: RSA keys shorter than 1024 bits can be broken, and verifiers reject them: the signatures are worth nothing.

data.name: DkimShortKeyTitle
data.value: 1024-bit DKIM key (selector {0}, {1} bit)

data.name: DkimShortKeyRisk
data.value: 1024-bit RSA keys are still accepted but below today's recommendation of 2048 bits.

data.name: DkimNewKeyFix
data.value: Generate a new 2048-bit key at your provider, publish it under a new selector, then remove the old one.

data.name: DkimTestingTitle
data.value: DKIM key in test mode (selector {0}, t=y)

data.name: DkimTestingRisk
data.value: Receivers may treat the signatures of a key in test mode as not verified.

data.name: DkimTestingFix
data.value: Remove t=y from the record when the test is over.

data.name: MxMissingTitle
data.value: No MX record

data.name: MxMissingRisk
data.value: The domain declares no mail server: mail sent to it goes to its web address or is lost, and the domain can still be forged.

data.name: MxMissingFix
data.value: If the domain receives mail, publish its MX records. If it does not, publish a null MX (0 .) together with v=spf1 -all and DMARC p=reject.

data.name: MxAddressLiteralTitle
data.value: MX that points to an IP address ({0})

data.name: MxAddressLiteralRisk
data.value: An MX must name a host, not an IP address: many senders will not deliver to it.

data.name: MxAddressLiteralFix
data.value: Create an A record for a host name (for example mail.<your domain>) and point the MX to that name.

data.name: MxUnresolvableTitle
data.value: Mail server without an address ({0})

data.name: MxUnresolvableRisk
data.value: A mail server listed in the MX has no address: mail can be delayed or lost.

data.name: MxUnresolvableFix
data.value: Correct the MX record, or publish the A/AAAA record of the host.

data.name: MxUnverifiedTitle
data.value: Mail server that could not be checked ({0})

data.name: MxUnverifiedFix
data.value: Run the check again later; if the error persists, check the DNS of the mail server with its provider.
